fundingamount: Up to 70% funding for job redesign activities and qualifying workforce transformation costs (exact quantum TBC as scheme rolls out)
fundingpercentage: Up to 70% funding for job redesign activities and qualifying workforce transformation costs (exact quantum TBC as scheme rolls out)
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-registered employer ② Active CPF contributors ③ Project must involve genuine workforce transformation outcomes ④ Full details TBC as scheme is progressively launched in 2026
supportedusecases: Job redesign, workforce planning, skills upgrading, career conversion, digital transformation upskilling, structured workplace learning
applicationprocess: 1. Apply via Business Grants Portal (BGP) — single channel 2. Engage Anchor Programme Partners for end-to-end advisory support 3. Implement transformation plan 4. Submit claim
requireddocuments: Details to be confirmed as WDG rolls out in 2026; expected to align with BGP standard documentation requirements
restrictions: Announced at Committee of Supply 2025. Consolidates WSG Career Conversion Programmes and SSG NACE Workplace Learning Projects. More details to be published as scheme launches progressively in 2026.

description: Supports startup accelerators and incubators to groom early-stage startups in Singapore. Provides funding for accelerator programme operations, mentorship, and startup development activities.
fundingamount: ESG co-funds qualifying accelerator programme costs. Quantum varies by programme scale and scope.
fundingpercentage: ESG co-funds qualifying accelerator programme costs. Quantum varies by programme scale and scope.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Incorporated in Singapore ② Operating a structured accelerator/incubator programme ③ Programme must have clear milestones, mentorship, and be focused on innovative startups ④ Must demonstrate track record or credible team
supportedusecases: Startup ecosystem development, mentorship programme operations, demo days, startup recruitment, curriculum development, investor access facilitation
applicationprocess: 1. Prepare programme proposal 2. Submit to Enterprise Singapore for evaluation 3. Await assessment and LOF 4. Implement programme 5. Submit claims with evidence
requireddocuments: Programme proposal; team credentials; startup cohort details; programme curriculum; cost breakdown
restrictions: Targeted at accelerator/incubator operators, not individual startups. Startups benefit indirectly through enrolled programmes. Visit EnterpriseSG for current programme list.

agency: Enterprise Singapore (ESG) via SEEDS Capital / SGInnovate / EDBI
description: Government co-invests alongside qualified third-party investors (VCs, angel investors) in early-stage startups. Two models: co-investment (SEEDS Capital/SGInnovate) and funds-of-funds (EDBI).
fundingamount: General tech: SEEDS Capital invests up to S$2M (7:3 ratio in first round, 1:1 up to S$2M). Deep tech: up to S$8M (7:3 first S$500K, 1:1 to S$4M, 3:7 beyond). Funds-of-funds: investee fund allocation up to 20% per company.
fundingpercentage: General tech: SEEDS Capital invests up to S$2M (7:3 ratio in first round, 1:1 up to S$2M). Deep tech: up to S$8M (7:3 first S$500K, 1:1 to S$4M, 3:7 beyond). Funds-of-funds: investee fund allocation up to 20% per company.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-based company with core operations here ② Must have secured qualified third-party investor (VC/angel) ③ Early-stage startup with innovative, scalable model ④ Deep tech focus for higher investment cap
supportedusecases: Early-stage startup funding, deep tech (advanced manufacturing, medtech, agrifood), tech commercialisation, scaling growth
applicationprocess: 1. Secure qualified third-party investor first 2. Submit 2-page executive summary + supporting documents 3. Submit via Startup SG Equity information page 4. SEEDS Capital / SGInnovate / EDBI assesses 5. Co-investment agreement
requireddocuments: 2-page executive summary; term sheet or LOI from third-party investor; business plan; cap table
restrictions: Company must secure third-party investor first — government does not invest alone. Equity stake dilution involved. Not a grant; structured as equity co-investment.

agency: Enterprise Singapore (ESG) via Accredited Mentor Partners (AMPs)
description: Provides mentorship and startup capital for first-time entrepreneurs with innovative, scalable business ideas. Two tracks: Train (pre-incorporation training) and Start (capital grant + mentorship).
fundingamount: S$20,000–S$50,000 on a 1:1 co-matching basis over 12 months (founders inject equal paid-up capital). Effective 1 Apr 2024.
fundingpercentage: S$20,000–S$50,000 on a 1:1 co-matching basis over 12 months (founders inject equal paid-up capital). Effective 1 Apr 2024.
eligibilitycriteria: ① ≥2 Singapore Citizen/PR founders holding ≥30% equity collectively ② Main applicant must be first-time founder (no prior Pte Ltd on ACRA) ③ Second applicant may be non-first-time founder (from 1 Apr 2024) ④ Pte Ltd incorporated in Singapore <6 months ⑤ Business idea must be novel, feasible, and scalable
supportedusecases: Prototype development, market research, early product commercialisation, talent hiring, innovation across tech, services, and manufacturing sectors
applicationprocess: 1. Choose an Accredited Mentor Partner (AMP) 2. Submit business proposal to AMP 3. AMP evaluates and recommends to ESG 4. ESG acknowledges within 5 working days 5. LOF issued if approved 6. Inject co-matching paid-up capital 7. 12-month mentorship with milestone-based disbursement
requireddocuments: Business proposal; ACRA bizfile; personal profiles of founders; proof of entrepreneurship training completed
restrictions: Excluded sectors: F&B (cafes/restaurants/bars), massage parlours, gambling, employment agencies, geomancy. Cannot combine with other government funding for same project. Previously funded SSGF recipients not eligible. Disbursed by milestones.

description: Accelerates commercialisation of proprietary technology solutions. Provides early-stage funding for breakthrough-level innovation with scalable tech-based business models. Carries an equity component.
fundingamount: Up to S$250,000 for Proof-of-Concept (POC); up to S$500,000 for Proof-of-Value (POV). ESG takes equity stake (share subscription right).
fundingpercentage: Up to S$250,000 for Proof-of-Concept (POC); up to S$500,000 for Proof-of-Value (POV). ESG takes equity stake (share subscription right).
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-incorporated company ② Group turnover ≤S$100M OR ≤200 employees ③ ≥30% local equity ④ Technology must be proprietary and breakthrough-level (disruptive or creates new market) ⑤ Must lead to or build on proprietary IP ⑥ Must be commercially viable
supportedusecases: Deep tech, medtech, agrifood tech, advanced manufacturing, AI/software, hardware innovation, proprietary technology commercialisation
applicationprocess: 1. Prepare executive summary + supporting documents 2. Submit via Startup SG Tech application form 3. Assessment by ESG 4. Milestone-based disbursement upon LOF acceptance
requireddocuments: Executive summary; business plan; IP documentation; prototype evidence (for POV); founding team credentials
restrictions: ESG retains right to exercise share subscription (equity component). Grant disbursed upon milestone completion. POC = concept stage; POV = proven concept requiring further development. Not for revenue-generating products.

grantname: Support for Job Redesign under Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG-JR)
description: Co-funds consultancy services to help companies redesign work processes, tasks, and responsibilities to optimise human capital.
fundingamount: Up to 70% of job redesign consultancy costs, capped at S$30,000 per enterprise.
fundingpercentage: Up to 70% of job redesign consultancy costs, capped at S$30,000 per enterprise.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; at least 3 local employees; must engage pre-approved Job Redesign consultants.
supportedusecases: Reviewing compensation structures, combining redundant roles into high-value positions, mapping new digital workflows.
applicationprocess: 1. Select pre-approved JR consultant. 2. Draft project scope. 3. Apply via BGP. 4. Implement and claim.
requireddocuments: Consultant proposal/quotation, ACRA Bizfile, CPF records showing existing workforce size.
restrictions: Focuses purely on the consultancy and workflow redesign phase, not the purchase of hardware (which requires standard PSG).

description: Wage offset scheme to support employers who hire local ex-offenders seeking workforce reintegration. Extended until 2028 (announced Budget 2025).
fundingamount: Up to 20% of employee's monthly wages, capped at S$600 per month per eligible employee, for the first 9 months of employment. Paid out annually in May via GIRO/PayNow Corporate.
fundingpercentage: Up to 20% of employee's monthly wages, capped at S$600 per month per eligible employee, for the first 9 months of employment. Paid out annually in May via GIRO/PayNow Corporate.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Registered employer in Singapore with valid GIRO or PayNow Corporate ② Hired Singapore Citizen or PR ex-offender ③ Ex-offender earning <S$4,000/month ④ Ex-offender released within 3 years prior to employment ⑤ Employer must make timely mandatory CPF contributions ⑥ Business owners (sole proprietors, partners, shareholder-directors) not eligible
supportedusecases: Hiring and reintegrating ex-offenders; inclusive employment; social responsibility hiring; industries with manpower needs (food services, logistics, cleaning)
applicationprocess: 1. Hire eligible ex-offender and make CPF contributions 2. Apply via go.gov.sg/applyUEC by 31 Jan of the following year 3. IRAS processes application 4. Payout credited in May of the following year via GIRO or PayNow Corporate
requireddocuments: Employment contract; CPF contribution records; ex-offender details for verification
restrictions: Applicable for ex-offenders hired from April 2023 – December 2028. No cheques issued. Payouts only via GIRO or PayNow Corporate. Business owners in own companies not eligible. Annual application deadline is 31 Jan of following year.

description: Co-funds commercial and industrial facilities to implement water recycling or water efficiency initiatives.
fundingamount: Up to 50% to 70% of project costs depending on the type of water recycling system or water-saving equipment installed.
fundingpercentage: Up to 50% to 70% of project costs depending on the type of water recycling system or water-saving equipment installed.
eligibilitycriteria: Non-domestic water users in SG; monthly water consumption must meet minimum PUB thresholds for the specific tier.
supportedusecases: Installing reverse osmosis recycling plants in semiconductor fabs, rainwater harvesting systems, cooling tower water optimization.
applicationprocess: 1. Conduct water audit. 2. Submit proposal to PUB. 3. Approval & Installation. 4. Post-installation audit & claim.
requireddocuments: Water efficiency audit report, engineering diagrams, vendor quotations, projected water savings metrics.
restrictions: Only funds projects that go beyond standard regulatory compliance; baseline water saving measures are not funded.

description: Encourages lower-wage workers (Singapore Citizens earning ≤S$2,500/month) to attend approved training courses. Employers receive absentee payroll funding; employees receive training allowances.
fundingamount: Up to 95% of course fees subsidised + 95% absentee payroll funding for employers (S$4.50/hr for courses ≤ CET framework; higher rates for specific programmes). Employees receive training allowances.
fundingpercentage: Up to 95% of course fees subsidised + 95% absentee payroll funding for employers (S$4.50/hr for courses ≤ CET framework; higher rates for specific programmes). Employees receive training allowances.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore Citizen employee ② Monthly wage ≤S$2,500 ③ Aged 30 and above (aged 35+ for Workfare Income Supplement) ④ Employed and actively working ⑤ Employer must support worker in attending approved WSQ or eligible training
supportedusecases: Lower-wage worker upskilling, WSQ certifications, skills upgrading, workforce capability building, adult education, sector-specific competency courses
applicationprocess: 1. Employee identifies and enrolls in approved WSQ/eligible course 2. Employer claims absentee payroll via SkillsFuture portal 3. Employee claims training allowance via CPF Board
requireddocuments: Employee CPF details; course enrolment proof; wage records
restrictions: Worker must be Singapore Citizen. Monthly wage cap S$2,500. Employer must maintain CPF contributions to qualify for absentee payroll. Training allowance disbursed by CPF Board.
